title: Сотейник в сейфе  (The Sauté Pan in the Safe)

segments.t: Back in the office at Claude Monet, German takes kitchen security to a ridiculous extreme by locking the copper sauté pan inside a heavy metal safe and pocketing the key.
Вам не кажется, что это перебор?
От него можно ожидать чего угодно.
Я всё-таки возьму ключики от сейфа.
Он не станет заниматься такой ерундой.
Let's go through Vika and German's exchange around the office safe.
'And your sauté pan is fine.' Focusing on the pan before German, Vika links the Russian words directly in the present with no word for "am", "is", or "are" needed.
Вам не кажется, что это перебор?
'Does it not seem to you that this is overkill?' Vika questions evenly where this conversation is heading next.
'He steals a defenseless sauté pan!' Mentioning the pan during the talk, German leans on "bezzashchitnyy" ("defenseless") to give the whole sentence its punch.
'And these are security measures.' Mentioning the safety with Vika, German links the Russian words directly in the present with no word for "am", "is", or "are" needed.

'Excuse me, what safe is this?' German plainly extends this formal apology in front of Vika using "prostite" ("forgive me") — a warmer, more earnest polite apology that literally asks someone to forgive you.
'It was left over from the old owners.' Emphasizing the owner with German, Vika brings in "khozyayev" ("owner, proprietor", from "khozyain") as the key Russian word here.
'I do not use it.' Looking over smoothly at once, the "-sya" ending on "polzuyus" ("I am taking advantage") marks an action that unfolds mutually or turns back on the speaker.
'Well, I will use it, give me the keys.' German opens up calmly across the room, refusing to let the moment slip past.
'Now that is another matter.' Focusing on the matter in this beat, German centers the thought on "drugoye" ("another, other", from "drugoy") without wasting a word.
'Do you think Viktor will try again?' Turning plainly on the spot, Vika keeps normal statement word order here, turning the line into a question for German purely through rising pitch.
От него можно ожидать чего угодно.
'You can expect anything at all from him.' German continues evenly on the spot, testing Vika's reaction in the middle of the exchange.
Я всё-таки возьму ключики от сейфа.
'I will take the spare keys to the safe after all.' Emphasizing the key before German, Vika puts the weight on "klyuchiki" ("little key", from "klyuchik") as the exchange unfolds.
'You do not use it, do you?' Reacting quietly beside Vika, the "-sya" ending on "polzuyetes" ("are taking advantage of") marks an action that unfolds mutually or turns back on the speaker.
Он не станет заниматься такой ерундой.
'He will not bother with such nonsense.' Vika opens up calmly watching German, grounding the moment in plain reality. Now let's hear the whole scene again from start to finish.
Вам не кажется, что это перебор?
От него можно ожидать чего угодно.
Я всё-таки возьму ключики от сейфа.
Он не станет заниматься такой ерундой.
That wraps up this scene as german locks the reclaimed copper sauté pan inside an old office safe to keep Barinov away from it, and Vika slyly asks to borrow the spare keys. See you next time!
